artworks.title: Achilles and Troilus
artworks.description: Roman marble group in the Naples National Archaeological Museum (inv. 5999), often read as Achilles seizing the boy Troilus. The warrior lifts the struggling youth — the ambush at the fountain that vase-painters made Troilus' defining death, here carved as a single fatal grasp.

artworks.title: Achilles Ambushing Troilus
artworks.description: Etruscan wall painting in the Tomb of the Bulls at Tarquinia. Achilles crouches in ambush as Troilus rides past on horseback — one of the earliest monumental images of the Trojan prince's death, painted more than a century before the Classical vase tradition fixed the fountain scene.

artworks.title: Achilles Lying in Wait for Troilus
artworks.artist: Attributed to the Painter of London B 76
artworks.description: Attic black-figure hydria in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (45.11.2). Achilles lurks behind the fountain as Troilus and Polyxena approach to water their horses — the ambush that ends the youth before Troy falls, already a favourite subject of sixth-century Athenian painters.

artworks.title: A Scene from Troilus and Cressida
artworks.description: Engraving by Luigi Schiavonetti after Angelica Kauffmann's 1789 painting of Shakespeare's Troilus and Cressida, Act V, Scene ii. Troilus watches as Cressida yields to Diomedes — the medieval romance of the Trojan prince restaged as bitter theatrical betrayal.

artworks.title: Troilus and Cressida in the Garden of Pandarus
artworks.description: Oil painting by the Victorian illustrator Edward Henry Corbould. Troilus and Cressida meet in Pandarus' garden — Chaucer's and Shakespeare's lovers before the war and the betrayal unmake them, the Trojan prince cast as courtly suitor rather than Achilles' victim.

films.title: The Face of Love
films.description: BBC modern-dress Troilus and Cressida: Laurence Payne's Troilus watches love turn to betrayal — Shakespeare's bitter Trojan comedy for early television.

music.title: Troilus and Cressida
music.description: Walton's Covent Garden opera after Chaucer gives Troilus a full-length lyric voice — the Trojan prince as betrayed lover rather than fountain victim.

popCulture.title: Troilus and Cressida
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's bitter Trojan comedy made Troilus the betrayed lover — medieval romance grafted onto the Iliad's doomed prince.

popCulture.title: Troilus and Criseyde
popCulture.creator: Geoffrey Chaucer
popCulture.description: Chaucer's long Middle English poem is Troilus' great medieval afterlife — courtly love, Criseyde's exchange, and the prince who dies still loving.

popCulture.title: Il Filostrato
popCulture.creator: Giovanni Boccaccio
popCulture.description: Boccaccio's ottava rima romance gave Chaucer his Troilus plot — the Trojan prince as love's prostrate victim before Shakespeare made him bitter.

popCulture.title: Troilus
popCulture.description: Achilles' ambush of the young Trojan at the fountain remains vase-painting's favourite Troilus scene — youth cut down before the war's end.
